messages:
sam: Heads-up — GHAS workflow started failing intermittently on the trivy scan step this morning. Seen a couple of repos with non-zero exit even though the findings look like low-severity noise. Anyone digging in? :thinking:

jamal: I noticed that too. The runner log shows `scanner returned exit code 1` after printing a long list of `UNSUPPORTED_ARCH` and a few CVE lines. Posting snippet: ```
INFO: running trivy filesystem...
2026-02-14T09:12:03Z ERROR: failed to scan: exit status 1
VULN: CVE-2022-XXXX  (LOW) 
VULN: CVE-2024-AAAA  (UNKNOWN)
```

maria: Are we using the same suppression rules that caused the earlier false positives? We had added a suppression file for package-lock noise last quarter. Could be misapplied in GHAS runner context.

alex: FYI deploy-bot shows the workflow run IDs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/actions/runs/987654321. Looks like the failures spike when multiple jobs run concurrently. Possible rate-limit or temp fs mount issue.

deploy-bot: [automation] workflow:ghas-trivy-scan #238 failed for redwood-inference/core at 2026-02-14T09:11:59Z (see run https://github.com/redwood-inference/actions/runs/987654321).

sam: Good catch on concurrency. Two threads of investigation: 1) why trivy returns non-zero on low/unknown findings (we should tolerate configurable exit codes), 2) why suppression rules aren't filtering the noise consistently. Prioritization: this blocks CI for some repos, so treat as P2 until we can make scans non-blocking.

nidhi: Quick workaround: adjust GHAS job to `continue-on-error: true` for trivy step while we triage. That reduces CI pain. Longer term we should set `--exit-code 0` and rely on annotations instead.

jamal: I agree. Also seeing `UNSUPPORTED_ARCH` in the logs — might be scanning build artifacts compiled for arm64 on x86 runner. Trivy may error when encountering unknown ELF headers. We should filter artifact paths or run platform-specific scanning.

maria: On suppression rules: here's the current suppression mapping we use in S3: `suppression.yml` contains patterns for `node_modules` and `go.sum` known fuzz. But GHAS uses a different workspace layout so suppr file isn't being picked up in some repos (path mismatch).

alex: Ops suggestion: add a small wrapper script for the trivy step: `./scripts/run-trivy.sh` that ensures the suppression file path and normalizes arch flags. Example snippet: ```bash
#!/bin/bash
export TRIVY_SUPPRESSION_FILE=.github/trivy/suppress.yml
trivy fs --exit-code 0 --format sarif --skip-update "$1"
```
That should avoid CI failures and produce SARIF for GHAS.

maria: We also need to decide CVE triage policy for auto-priority vs manual. My proposal: auto-mark as "low-priority" if CVSS < 6.0 and no exploitability metadata; auto-high if CVSS >= 9.0 or exploit proof-of-concept exists. Everything else queue for manual triage. Thoughts?

sam: That policy sounds reasonable. For this thread, the failing CVEs are mostly UNKNOWN/LOW and being caught due to path mismatch, so treat as noise until we confirm reproducible exploitability.

nidhi: Regarding KMS/artifact questions — some folks asked whether trivy needs access to KMS to decrypt private artifacts. It doesn't. We unpack build artifacts before scan; the runner should mount decrypted files. If anyone wired trivy to call our KMS, let's revert that. Keep scanning as a post-decrypt step.

jamal: Action items I can take: 1) Add `continue-on-error: true` and wrapper script to the GHAS workflow (PR incoming), 2) Add runner label `self-hosted-arm64` to avoid arch mismatches where relevant, 3) Add a sanity check that suppression file exists before scanning.

alex: I'll review the PR. Also let's add a metric/alert in Console for "scan-failed" > 5% of runs in 1h so we detect regressions.

maria: For suppression rules hygiene — I'll audit the suppression.yml patterns and remove overly broad regexes that masked real findings last quarter. Will push a cleaned file and update docs for where GHAS expects it.

sam: Great. Low-risk mitigation: implement wrapper + continue-on-error now. Medium-term: platform change to have trivy run in a dedicated step that writes SARIF and returns 0 while failing the GHAS check only if any HIGH/Critical above threshold.

deploy-bot: [reminder] @sam @maria @jamal PR #1542 for `ghas-trivy-scan` wrapper created by jamal, status: open. https://github.com/redwood-inference/pipelines/pull/1542

sam: Perfect. If anyone spots a repo where an actual HIGH CVE is being suppressed wrongly, ping immediately and mark it P0. Otherwise we'll roll the fix and monitor. :thumbsup:
